classification.difficultyReason: Find the missing perpendicular side using Pythagoras’ theorem, then calculate the triangle’s area.

content.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse of length $41\text{ cm}$ and one of the sides is $9\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the triangle.

answer.short:
$180\text{ cm}^2$.

Pythagoras’ theorem gives the other perpendicular side as $40\text{ cm}$; use the two perpendicular sides as base and height.
answer.worked:
Let $b$ be the other perpendicular side, measured in centimetres. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}b^2+9^2&=41^2\\b^2+81&=1681\\b^2&=1681-81\\b^2&=1600\\b&=40\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular sides are the base and height, so
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times9\times40\\A&=180\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
